assessment.title: Cell death, senescence, and the failure of a renewal loop

items.prompt: A crypt of the human descending colon holds about 700 cells. Treat its renewal as complete replacement of that population over 4 days, and treat the crypt's cell number as steady. How many cells must leave that one crypt per day? Give your answer in cells per day, to the nearest 5.

answer.reasoning: Complete replacement of 700 cells over 4 days means about 700 / 4 = 175 cells produced per day. The crypt's number is steady, and a steady population requires loss to match production on average, so about 175 cells must also leave per day. Both halves of the answer are needed: the division gives the production rate, and the balance condition transfers it to the loss rate. Note what the figure is and is not. It is a population rate for one crypt under the stated assumptions, and it is not a claim that each crypt cell lives exactly 4 days; the renewal interval reported for the colon is a range of 3 to 5 days, and 4 is the working value the stem supplies.
commonErrors: Answering 700 by giving the population instead of a rate; the question asks how many cells leave per day, which is a rate, and the population is the quantity that stays constant.
Answering 2800 by multiplying 700 by 4 instead of dividing; check the direction by confirming that 175 x 4 = 700, which is the whole population replaced in the stated interval.
Answering 0 on the grounds that the crypt's cell number does not change; a constant population means production and loss are equal, not that either is zero.
Giving a production figure but not connecting it to loss; the balance condition is the step that answers the question as asked.

items.prompt: A colonic epithelial cell has died. Which single observation best distinguishes apoptosis from a death in which the cell lost plasma membrane integrity?

options.text: The cell had permanently stopped dividing before it died.
The cell's contents stayed inside membrane-bounded fragments, and neighbouring cells cleared them with no inflammatory infiltrate present.
The cell had detached from the basement membrane before it died.

answer.summary: The contents stayed inside membrane-bounded fragments and were cleared without inflammation.
answer.reasoning: This is the discriminating observation because it names the two consequences that differ. An apoptotic cell retains an intact plasma membrane, so its cytoplasmic contents are not released into the interstitium, and essentially no inflammatory reaction accompanies the process. Where membrane integrity is lost instead, contents go out into the surrounding tissue, chemotactic signals follow, inflammatory cells are recruited, and inflammation is usually present. Containment and the absence of an infiltrate therefore separate the two, and they are the pair of features that matters to a sheet whose job is to stay sealed.
commonErrors: Choosing permanent arrest before death confuses senescence with apoptosis. A senescent cell has stopped dividing and has not died or been removed, so this observation belongs to a different state entirely.

Choosing prior detachment confuses the trigger with the mode of death. Detachment can start apoptosis, which is anoikis, but detachment does not tell you whether the death that followed contained the cell's contents, and whether death precedes or follows detachment at an intestinal surface is not settled.
Choosing DNA damage names a possible cause of either outcome and so discriminates between neither.

items.prompt: A cell in a tissue has entered cellular senescence. Select every statement this lesson's sources support.

options.text: Its arrest of proliferation is essentially irreversible.
It has been removed from the tissue.
It remains viable and metabolically active, and many senescent cells secrete a programme of proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors and proteases.
The response it has entered can both constrain the development of malignant tumours and contribute to age-related pathology.
It is simply a cell that has aged and worn out.

answer.summary: The arrest is essentially irreversible; the cell stays active and secreting; and the response works in both directions.
answer.reasoning:
Cellular senescence is defined as the essentially irreversible arrest of cell proliferation entered when a cell experiences potentially oncogenic stress, and senescent cells remain viable and metabolically active. They display the senescence-associated secretory phenotype, secreting proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors and proteases. The permanence of the arrest is why the response is read as suppressing cancer development, while the same response may act as a basic ageing process driving age-related pathology later in life, and its secretions can make a local environment permissive for cancer. All three of those are supported and the tension between the last two is not a contradiction to be resolved.

Note for the marker on the secretion option. Viability and metabolic activity are defining features within this lesson's model. The secretory programme is not: its composition varies with cell type, with what caused the arrest, and with time since it began, so an answer that treats it as a guaranteed identical property of every senescent cell is overstating it. The option is worded as many senescent cells for that reason, and a learner who selects it while noting the heterogeneity has given the better answer.
commonErrors: Selecting that the cell has been removed from the tissue confuses senescence with apoptosis. Removal is what apoptosis achieves; senescence leaves the cell in place, which is the whole reason its secretions matter.

Selecting that it is simply an aged, worn-out cell is the most common error and the one the scene was written against. The triggers are damage and inappropriate signalling, including oncogene activation, and elapsed time is not the definition. Telomere shortening is one trigger on a list of several.
Selecting only the arrest and omitting the secretory phenotype gets the definition and misses the consequence, which is where both halves of the senescence account come from.

Declining to select the two-directional statement because it seems self-contradictory. Both effects are supported, and the framework for holding them together is that a response beneficial at one stage of life can carry costs at another.

items.prompt: In the 2015 study this lesson uses, about a quarter of the cells in normal, visibly unremarkable, functioning eyelid epidermis carried a NOTCH driver mutation, and some clones carried two or three driver mutations without having acquired malignant potential. In two or three sentences, state what this result rules out, and then state one thing it does not establish.

answer.correct: It rules out the claim that carrying a driver mutation is sufficient to make a cell a cancer cell, because a quarter of a functioning epidermis carried one and that tissue was not cancer. It does not establish that driver mutations are unnecessary, and it does not establish anything about the colon, since the study sampled sun-exposed eyelid skin from four donors.
answer.summary: It rules out sufficiency, not necessity; and it is skin from four donors, not colon.
answer.reasoning: The result is a counterexample to one proposition and to no others. If a driver mutation were sufficient for a cell to be a cancer cell, then a tissue in which about a quarter of cells carried one could not be normal, functioning epidermis free of visible lesions. It was, so sufficiency fails. Necessity is untouched: the same body of work has a typical tumour carrying two to eight driver mutations, so drivers remain part of the account. And the scope limits are real. Four donors, one heavily sun-exposed site, and skin rather than colon, so the numbers should not be read as general values for human tissue and this lesson holds no colonic dataset of the same kind. Any one of those three limits is a correct answer to the second half.
acceptableResponses: It rules out that a driver mutation is enough on its own to produce cancer; it does not show drivers are unnecessary.
Carrying a cancer driver mutation is not sufficient for cancer. It does not tell you the same fractions apply to the colon, because the study was eyelid skin.
A driver mutation alone does not make a tumour, since the epidermis worked normally. The study cannot establish general mutant-cell fractions from four donors.
It rules out mutation being sufficient. It does not establish what the tissue contributes, only that something besides the mutation must be involved.
commonErrors: Concluding that driver mutations do not matter, or that mutation is irrelevant to cancer. The result bears on sufficiency and leaves necessity intact; a typical tumour carries two to eight drivers.

Concluding that the donors were developing cancer or were at stated risk. The study describes what the sampled tissue contained and supports no statement about any person's risk, and this lesson makes none.
Transferring the quarter-of-cells figure to the colon or to skin generally. It comes from sun-exposed eyelid epidermis in four donors aged 55 to 73.
Stating only what the result rules out and omitting a limit, which answers half the question.

items.prompt: A study reported three things. Most cells extruded from epithelia during ordinary homeostasis were caspase-negative, so still alive as they left. Blocking stretch-activated channels or knocking down Piezo1 in zebrafish reduced extrusion and produced epidermal cell masses, with cell density staying elevated. And colon polyp sections showed increased cell density with no clearly identified extrusion events, compared with control sections. Which conclusion do these results support?

options.text: Failure of crowding-induced extrusion causes colorectal cancer.
Crowding-induced extrusion removes cells from an epithelium, and preventing it allowed cells to accumulate in zebrafish epidermis.
Colon polyps form because their cells lack Piezo1.
Only cells that have already died are extruded from an epithelium.

answer.summary: Extrusion removes cells, and blocking it let cells accumulate in zebrafish.
answer.reasoning: This is the conclusion the described results actually license. The mechanical role of extrusion in controlling cell number is what the crowding experiments demonstrate, and the cell masses with sustained elevated density are the demonstrated consequence of blocking it in zebrafish. Both statements stay inside what was measured and inside the system it was measured in.
commonErrors: Choosing that extrusion failure causes colorectal cancer overreads the polyp observation. That observation is a difference in density and in identified extrusions between polyp and control sections, examined once, which is an association. The authors themselves offer the tumour connection as a suggestion rather than a result, and a demonstrated causal chain would need the order of events and an intervention.

Choosing that polyps form because their cells lack Piezo1 imports the zebrafish manipulation into human tissue as an explanation. Piezo1 was knocked down experimentally in zebrafish; nothing described here measured Piezo1 in a polyp.

Choosing that only already-dead cells are extruded contradicts the first result. Most extrusions during homeostasis were caspase-negative, meaning the cells were alive as they left, which is the finding that makes extrusion separable from death.

items.prompt: A research preparation of colonic epithelium has cell density above its control. Apoptotic cells are present at the surface at the usual frequency, with condensed nuclei and intact membranes, and they are being cleared with no inflammatory infiltrate. Every cell in the sheet is still attached to its basement membrane. Name the controls of the renewal loop that appear to be operating, name every part of the loop where the imbalance could still sit, and state one thing this description does not let you decide.

answer.correct: The apoptotic programme and the clearance of apoptotic cells are operating, shown by cells with condensed nuclei and intact membranes being removed without an inflammatory infiltrate. Attachment is intact, so nothing has detached and attachment-dependent death is untested here. The imbalance could still sit in raised production at the base, in cells failing to stop dividing and differentiate on the climb, or in failed extrusion of live cells, because the description reports no extrusion events and extrusion is separable from apoptosis. What it does not let you decide is which of those three, because a density is a state and the imbalance is a rate.
answer.summary: Apoptosis, clearance and attachment are intact; the imbalance could still be raised production, a climb that does not end, or failed live-cell extrusion; the snapshot cannot separate them.
answer.reasoning: Three moves. First, identify the intact controls from what is stated: the apoptotic morphology with the absence of an inflammatory infiltrate shows the programme running and the clearance working, and every cell being attached shows the basal adhesion is in place, which also means attachment-dependent survival has not been tested here. Second, apply the balance relation: cell number rises exactly as fast as production exceeds loss, so something is out of balance. Third, and this is the step the item is really testing, do not narrow it further than the description allows. Apoptosis is not the whole of removal. Scene 3 established that extrusion is separable from death, so a sheet can fail to extrude live cells when it becomes crowded while its apoptotic machinery works perfectly, and this description reports no extrusion events at all. Raised production, a climb that does not end, and failed live-cell extrusion are therefore all consistent with what is stated. Any genuine limit earns the last mark: that a density is a state while the imbalance is a rate and so cannot be attributed from one snapshot; that attachment-dependent survival is untested because nothing has detached; or that the description contains no genomic information and so supports no statement about mutations.
acceptableResponses: Apoptosis, clearance and attachment are all operating. The imbalance could be raised production, a climb that does not end, or failed extrusion of live cells, and the description cannot separate them because a density is a state and the imbalance is a rate.

The death programme and its clearance work, and the cells are still attached so anoikis is untested. Removal by apoptosis looks fine but extrusion is unreported, so the excess could be on either side of the loop.

Apoptotic removal is intact, so a failure of the death programme is what this argues against. It does not narrow the imbalance further, since failed live-cell extrusion is still consistent with everything described.
commonErrors: Concluding that the imbalance must be on the production side. This is the most instructive wrong answer in the lesson and it comes from treating apoptosis as the whole of removal. Extrusion is a separate removal route, the description reports none, and a sheet can fail to extrude live cells while its apoptotic machinery works perfectly.
Concluding that the apoptotic programme has failed. The description says apoptotic cells are present at the usual frequency and are being cleared normally, which is evidence that it is operating.

Concluding that anoikis has been lost. Nothing in the sheet has detached, so attachment-dependent survival has not been put to the test here; this is a control that is untested rather than intact or broken, and saying so earns credit.

claims.uncertainty: Nomenclature is revised periodically and this is the 2018 revision. The lesson uses it for the accidental-versus-regulated distinction and for the point that morphology does not settle mechanism, both of which have been stable across revisions.

claims.statement: Disruption of the interactions between normal epithelial cells and extracellular matrix induced apoptosis in MDCK epithelial cells, and the authors named the phenomenon anoikis; sensitivity to it was regulated rather than universal, since it did not occur in normal fibroblasts and was abrogated in epithelial cells by transformation with v-Ha-ras or v-src or by phorbol-ester treatment, while overexpression of bcl-2 protected cells against it, leading the authors to suggest that circumvention of anoikis accompanies the acquisition of anchorage independence or cell motility.
claims.scope: MDCK epithelial cells derived from dog kidney, in culture, with matrix attachment removed experimentally, reported in 1994. The lesson states that species, preparation and date wherever the result is used.
claims.uncertainty: A cell-culture result. It establishes that epithelial survival can be attachment-dependent and that the dependence can be broken by specific changes; it does not establish what happens at the top of a human colonic crypt, and the lesson says so. The authors' closing statement about anchorage independence and motility is their suggestion, not a demonstrated link to disease.

claims.statement: Anoikis, Greek for homelessness, names a specialised form of apoptosis that follows loss of attachment to the native matrix, and inappropriate loss of anoikis is thought to facilitate the movement of cells to remote sites as occurs during metastasis of cancer cells; epithelial cell anoikis was found to be bypassed by oncogenic Ras or Src.
claims.scope: A 2008 review of mechanotransduction and anoikis. The etymology is taken from here because the 1994 paper that coined the term does not supply it.
claims.uncertainty: The review's own verb is that loss of anoikis is thought to facilitate movement of cells to remote sites, which is a proposed contribution and not a demonstrated one. The lesson preserves that hedge in prose and states that surviving detachment in culture is a long way short of a disease.

claims.statement: Cells are lost from the small-intestinal villus tip in a region called the extrusion zone, and it is not known whether cell death precedes the initiation of detachment or whether detachment itself causes the death, the second of these being anoikis, defined as programmed cell death following loss of anchorage-dependent survival signals; the same review reports evidence that the apoptotic pathway appears to be activated before cells reach the extrusion zone.
claims.scope: The small-intestinal villus tip, as reviewed in 2015. The claim is that the ordering question is open in the literature, and the review states this explicitly while reporting evidence on both sides.
claims.uncertainty: This is the lesson's central declared uncertainty. No assessment item in this pack has a key that depends on the ordering being settled, and the lesson states in prose that anoikis as the trigger for shedding at an intestinal surface is a candidate mechanism with contrary evidence beside it. The review concerns the small intestine, not the colon.

claims.statement: Tight junction protein zonula occludens 1 redistributes approximately fifteen minutes before an intestinal epithelial cell is shed, the epithelial gaps that develop after a cell is shed are sealed by neighbouring cells re-forming tight junctions within about twenty minutes, and an estimated 1400 mature enterocytes are shed from a single small-intestinal villus tip in each 24-hour period.
claims.scope: Small-intestinal villus-tip shedding, as reviewed in 2015, drawing substantially on mouse work. The lesson states the small-intestinal scope wherever these figures appear.
claims.uncertainty: The per-villus shedding estimate is explicitly an estimate and is small-intestinal; the lesson does not transfer it to the colon, which has a differently arranged surface. The timings are measurements from imaging studies the review collects and vary between preparations.

claims.statement: Overcrowding of an epithelium induces extrusion of live cells, which returns cell number towards its previous level; extruded cells were caspase-negative in 80 per cent of extrusions from human colon sections, 88 per cent from zebrafish epidermis and 67 per cent from cultured monolayers, and extrusion required stretch-activated ion channels, with the channel Piezo1 shown to regulate it in zebrafish.
claims.scope: Zebrafish epidermis in vivo, MDCK monolayers on stretchable membranes, and immunostained sections of normal human colon epithelium, reported in 2012.
claims.uncertainty: The mechanical extrusion step is demonstrated. The authors' proposal that most extruded cells subsequently die from anoikis through loss of matrix survival signals is their interpretation and was not demonstrated in the animal, and the lesson marks it as such wherever it appears. The human component is immunostained sections rather than live imaging.

claims.statement: Blocking crowding-induced extrusion produced epidermal cell masses in zebrafish, at fin edges after gadolinium treatment and at fin edges and other sites of tissue strain in Piezo1 morphants, with cell density remaining elevated where control tissue's density recovered; the authors suggest such masses may set the stage for tumourigenesis by allowing retention of oncogenic or defective cells, and report increased cell densities and no clearly identified extrusions in colon polyp sections compared with control sections.
claims.scope: Zebrafish epidermis for the masses and the density measurements; immunostained human colon polyp and control sections for the comparison. Reported in 2012.
claims.uncertainty: The masses following blocked extrusion in zebrafish are a demonstrated result. The link to tumour formation is explicitly the authors' suggestion, supported only by a difference between polyp and control sections, which is an association in tissue examined once and not a demonstrated causal chain. The lesson states this distinction where the claim is used and does not key any assessment item to the causal reading.

claims.statement: Cellular senescence is the essentially irreversible arrest of cell proliferation that occurs when cells experience potentially oncogenic stress, and senescent cells remain viable and metabolically active.
claims.scope: Mammalian cells, as defined in a 2013 review of ageing, cellular senescence and cancer.
claims.uncertainty: The review's own qualifier is essentially irreversible rather than absolutely irreversible, and the lesson keeps that wording rather than strengthening it. Much of the underlying characterisation comes from cultured cells and from mouse models.

claims.statement: Senescence is triggered by telomere shortening producing dysfunctional telomeres, by genomic damage including DNA double-strand breaks, by oncogene activation in a response termed oncogene-induced senescence, by epigenomic perturbations, and by mitogenic signals.
claims.scope: Mammalian cells, as collected in a 2013 review.
claims.uncertainty: A list of established triggers rather than an exhaustive one, and the relative contribution of each differs between cell types and settings. The lesson uses the list to make one point, that the category is defined by the trigger being oncogenic stress rather than by elapsed time, and claims nothing about which trigger dominates anywhere.

claims.statement: The permanence of the senescence growth arrest supports the view that the senescence response evolved at least in part to suppress the development of cancer, and senescence acts as a strong constraint on malignant tumour formation.
claims.scope: Mammalian cells and tissues, as argued in a 2013 review.
claims.uncertainty: The evolutionary reading is an inference the review draws from the permanence of the arrest rather than a directly measured result, and the lesson presents it as a reading. The tumour-suppressive function itself is well supported across cell and animal work.

claims.statement: Senescent cells display a senescence-associated secretory phenotype, secreting numerous proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors and proteases.
claims.scope: Senescent mammalian cells, as characterised in a 2013 review.
claims.uncertainty: The composition of the secreted set varies with cell type and with how senescence was induced; the lesson names the classes of molecule and no individual factor, and makes no claim about the amount secreted in any tissue.

claims.statement: Senescence may act as a basic ageing process that drives ageing phenotypes and age-related pathology late in life, and the senescence-associated secretory phenotype can promote the development of cancer by sustaining chronic inflammation and creating a permissive local environment, so the same response both constrains tumour development and can encourage it depending on when it occurs and what else is present.
claims.scope: Mammalian ageing and tumour biology, as argued in a 2013 review that presents this two-directional account within the antagonistic-pleiotropy framework.
claims.uncertainty: The review presents the late-life ageing role and the cancer-promoting role of the secretory phenotype as an argued account with supporting evidence rather than as settled fact, and the strength of evidence differs between the two halves. The lesson holds both effects open rather than resolving them, states no magnitude for either, and makes no claim about any individual's ageing or cancer risk.

claims.statement: It takes decades to develop a full-blown, metastatic cancer, and a colorectal tumour in a 90-year-old patient has nearly twice as many mutations as a morphologically identical colorectal tumour in a 45-year-old patient.
claims.scope: Human solid tumours as synthesised from sequencing studies in a 2013 review, with the age comparison specific to colorectal tumours.
claims.uncertainty: A statement about typical timescales across studied tumours, not about any individual course. The lesson uses it only to establish that the process is slow and cumulative, and draws no prognostic or personal conclusion from it.

claims.statement: About 93 per cent of colorectal cancers contain an activating mutation in the WNT pathway, particularly in APC, and APC mutations impair the destruction complex, leading to accumulation of beta-catenin; colorectal cancer is described as following a stepwise acquisition of characterised genetic mutations referred to as the adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence, and gatekeeping mutations in the colon most often occur in APC with mutations in KRAS and other genes following.
claims.scope: Human colorectal cancer at population level, from a 2025 review of the colonic crypt and a 2013 review of cancer genome landscapes. The 93 per cent figure and the destruction-complex consequence are adopted unchanged from PREM-BIO-006, which owns this material.
claims.uncertainty: A population figure from reviews and not anyone's personal risk, as PREM-BIO-006 also stated. The lesson makes no claim about how the sequence is detected, staged or managed, which this module's syllabus excludes.

claims.statement: Reorientation of the beta-catenin destruction complex towards a localised Wnt cue in cultured human colon epithelial cells requires full-length APC. A cell with damaged APC therefore accumulates beta-catenin and runs the beta-catenin-dependent gene programme whether or not Wnt is present, so its readout of position is decoupled from the gradient the crypt uses to signal height.
claims.scope: Human colon epithelial cell lines for the relocation requirement, and a 2025 review of the colonic crypt for the pathway consequence of APC loss. The first half is PREM-BIO-006's established conclusion, adopted here; the second half, that the climb therefore does not end in a departing cell, is this lesson's inference from it.
claims.uncertainty: What the sources measured is the decoupling of pathway output from Wnt input, in cultured colon epithelial models. They did not measure whether such a cell divides at every height, whether it ever differentiates, or whether it fails to become a departing cell. Those are this lesson's inferences from the content of the gene programme, and they are stated as inferences wherever they appear rather than as observed outcomes.

claims.statement: A typical tumour contains two to eight driver-gene mutations conferring a selective growth advantage, with the remaining mutations being passengers that confer none; in common adult tumours including colorectal, breast and brain cancers the number of mutated driver genes is often three to six; more than 99.9 per cent of the alterations in tumours are immaterial to neoplasia; an average of 33 to 66 genes display subtle somatic mutations expected to alter their protein products in common solid tumours of the colon, breast, brain or pancreas; and a benign tumour is defined as an abnormal proliferation of cells driven by at least one mutation.
claims.scope: Human tumours as synthesised from sequencing studies available in 2013.
claims.uncertainty: Driver-gene counts depend on how a driver is identified, and the review sets out its own criteria for that. The figures are averages and ranges across studied tumours, and the lesson uses them to compare orders of magnitude against mutation counts in normal tissue rather than as exact constants.

claims.statement: p53 is a cellular stress sensor that triggers transient cell-cycle arrest, permanent cell-cycle arrest as cellular senescence, and apoptosis in response to diverse stresses including DNA damage and hyperproliferative signals, and TP53 is inactivated in more than half of all sporadic human cancers.
claims.scope: Human and mouse p53 biology as synthesised in a 2014 review; the inactivation frequency is across sporadic human cancers collectively.
claims.uncertainty: The frequency is a population figure across cancer types and varies widely between them; the lesson states it as a collective figure and derives no personal or type-specific claim from it.

claims.statement: The downstream genes and pathways that are important for p53-mediated tumour suppression remain unresolved, and depending on the tissue either the cell-cycle arrest function or the apoptosis function of p53 can be the one that is vital for tumour suppression.
claims.scope: p53-mediated tumour suppression as assessed in a 2014 review, drawing largely on mouse genetic models.
claims.uncertainty: This claim is a statement that a question is open, and it is used in the lesson for exactly that: no assessment item keys which p53 response carries tumour suppression, because the review states it is unresolved. Later work may narrow it; the claim should be re-checked against current literature at review.

claims.statement: In 234 biopsies of sun-exposed eyelid epidermis from four donors aged 55 to 73, described as normal epidermis free of macroscopic lesions and maintaining the physiological functions of epidermis, mutations under positive selection were present in NOTCH1 in 14 to 21 per cent of skin cells, NOTCH2 in 5 to 7 per cent and NOTCH3 in 2 to 3 per cent, giving about a quarter of skin cells carrying a NOTCH mutation, with TP53 and FAT1 mutations each in 3 to 5 per cent; normal cells carried an average of 0.27 driver point mutations per cell with a 95 per cent confidence interval of 0.19 to 0.35; and the authors report clones carrying two to three driver mutations that had not acquired malignant potential, raising the question of what combinations of events are sufficient for transformation.
claims.scope: Sun-exposed eyelid epidermis from four donors aged 55 to 73, sequenced in a 2015 study. Skin, not colon, and a small number of donors; the lesson states both limits wherever the finding is used.
claims.uncertainty: Four donors and one heavily sun-exposed site, so the mutant-cell fractions should not be read as general values for human skin, still less for other tissues. This pack contains no equivalent dataset for the colon, so the lesson's extension of the finding to colonic crypts is presented explicitly as a use of the model and not as a reported measurement. No personal risk figure is derived from the study.

claims.statement: Cells in the lower half of the human colonic crypt migrate upward at an average speed of around 4 micrometres per hour.
claims.scope: Adopted from PREM-BIO-006, which established it from the same source. Used here only to set the pace of the climb the loop describes.
claims.uncertainty: The figure is reported for the lower half of the crypt only, where most of the study's sections were collected, and the lesson does not extend it over the whole climb. The comparison with a 10-micrometre cell diameter is the lesson's own arithmetic and is presented as an estimate.

terms.definition: A form of cell death the dying cell carries out itself, using machinery it already contains. The cell condenses, breaks into membrane-bounded fragments that keep its contents inside them, and is cleared by neighbouring or phagocytic cells or shed from an epithelial surface, without provoking an inflammatory response. The word names a programme rather than a degree of injury: a cell running it has been switched on, not overwhelmed. Do not treat it as interchangeable with programmed cell death, which is the wider category it belongs to.

In the usage recommended by the Nomenclature Committee on Cell Death, the regulated forms of cell death that run in ordinary physiology, without any perturbation from outside the organism. Apoptosis is one of them and is the one this lesson develops, so the two words are not synonyms: programmed cell death is the category and apoptosis is a member of it.

Cell death that depends on a dedicated molecular machinery, and which can therefore be delayed or accelerated by a genetic or pharmacological intervention. That modulability is the test: if interfering with a component changes the death, the death was regulated. Regulated cell death includes forms whose end result looks necrotic, so the category is defined by mechanism and not by appearance.

The immediate and catastrophic end of a cell exposed to a severe physical, chemical or mechanical insult. No dedicated pathway is involved, so no intervention in the cell's machinery delays it. This is the category that genuinely contrasts with regulated cell death.

A description of how a dead cell looks: swollen, with its plasma membrane given way and its contents released into the surrounding tissue, usually with inflammation present. The word names an appearance and not a cause. A necrotic-looking death may have been accidental or may have run through a dedicated pathway such as necroptosis or pyroptosis, and a tissue section alone does not distinguish those.

One of a family of cysteine proteases that carry out apoptosis. They divide by function into initiators, which respond to the signal that starts the process, and executioners, which do the disassembly. This lesson uses the two functional groups and the two routes that reach them, and treats the individual caspase numbers as a lookup rather than as material to hold.

Apoptosis triggered by the loss of, or by inappropriate, attachment between a cell and the extracellular matrix. The same execution machinery as any other apoptosis, reached from a different starting condition: the cell finds itself somewhere it should not be. The name is Greek for homelessness. In the human intestinal crypt, integrin receptors are reported to have a central role in controlling it; whether it is what triggers shedding at an intestinal surface is not settled.

The squeezing of a single cell out of an epithelial sheet by its neighbours, which close the gap behind it. PREM-BIO-007 used the word once without defining it, and this is the sense meant. Extrusion is a mechanical removal and is separable from death: a cell may be dead before it goes, or alive as it goes and die afterwards. Crowding of the sheet is one thing that drives it.

An essentially irreversible arrest of cell proliferation, entered when a cell experiences stress of a kind that could otherwise make it cancerous. The cell stays viable and metabolically active and is not removed. Two cautions on the word. It does not mean an old cell: the triggers are damage and inappropriate signalling, and elapsed time is not the definition. And parts of the intestinal literature use senescent loosely for worn-out surface cells about to be shed, which is the everyday sense and not this one.

The secretion by senescent cells of numerous proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, growth factors and proteases into the surrounding tissue. It is why a senescent cell is not a quiet one, and it carries both halves of the senescence account: the arrest constrains tumour development, while sustained secretion contributes to age-related pathology and can make the local environment permissive for cancer.

The permanent proliferative arrest a cell may enter in response to activation of an oncogene. The change that ought to make the cell divide without limit instead stops it dividing at all, which is why senescence is read as a response that suppresses cancer rather than as a failure of the cell.

A mutation that confers a selective growth advantage on the cell carrying it. A typical tumour contains two to eight of them. Carrying one is not the same as being a cancer: normal, functioning tissue can carry driver mutations in a large share of its cells, so a driver mutation is necessary for the process and not sufficient for the disease.

A mutation present in a tumour that confers no selective growth advantage, carried along by the clone rather than contributing to it. More than 99.9 per cent of the alterations found in tumours are immaterial to the disease, which is why finding a mutation in a tumour is not evidence that the mutation did anything.

The growth of a population of cells descended from one ancestor, because that ancestor acquired an advantage over its neighbours. Normal ageing tissue contains many such expansions at once, most of which never become anything else.

An abnormal proliferation of cells. A benign tumour is defined for this lesson as an abnormal proliferation driven by at least one mutation. This lesson uses the word structurally, for a growth that the renewal loop no longer removes, and does not treat it as a diagnosis or attach any clinical meaning to it.

A gene whose activation contributes to the growth advantage of a cell. In this lesson oncogenes appear twice and in opposite directions: introducing v-Ha-ras or v-src into epithelial cells abolished their attachment-dependent death, while activating an oncogene can also drive a cell into permanent arrest. Which of those a cell does is not decided by the oncogene alone.

A protein that senses cellular stress, including DNA damage and excessive proliferative signalling, and can produce transient cell-cycle arrest, permanent arrest as senescence, or apoptosis. It therefore sits at the junction of all three routes this lesson describes. The gene encoding it is written TP53, and the two names are not interchangeable: TP53 is the gene and p53 the protein. TP53 is inactivated in more than half of all sporadic human cancers, and which of p53's three responses does the tumour-suppressing work is not a settled question and depends on the tissue.

The sheet of extracellular material an epithelium sits on, containing laminins, fibronectin, collagen and other matrix components, which the cells above it grip through integrins. Despite the name it is not a lipid bilayer; it is secreted matrix lying outside the cell rather than enclosing it. In this lesson it is the surface whose loss anoikis responds to, which is why the term is repeated rather than assumed.

alignment.note: PREM-BIO-007 defines basement membrane for this course and this lesson keeps that meaning without alteration, including its warning that the word membrane is doing a different job here from the lipid-bilayer sense PREM-BIO-004 owns. Nothing is narrowed or extended. The entry is repeated rather than assumed because attachment to this specific structure is the survival condition anoikis reports on, and a reader who has forgotten which sheet is meant cannot follow scene 3.

attributionHtml:
Attribution and rights

Lesson content

Lesson PREM-BIO-010, "When the climb stops ending: cell death, senescence, and cancer", version 0.1.0, is licensed CC BY 4.0 as part of the EmbeddedKnowledge Premed corpus.

The accountable principal is VSBDev (github:VSBDev), verified in this run with gh api user.

Material agent assistance was used to draft the pack and is disclosed in lesson.json rather than hidden. The agent system, provider, model, version and run identifier are recorded as the literal RUNTIME-STAMPED because this authoring run could not verify them from inside itself; the operator stamps them. No value for any of those fields has been guessed. The instructionsDigest is a genuine SHA-256 over the discloseable material instructions supplied to this run, which were the cell-biology block brief and the lesson-specific task instructions. Its scope is those two documents and nothing more: it does not cover provider or harness system instructions, which this run cannot export.

This run performed authorship only. It produced no review artifact, no adjudication.json, no commit, no branch and no pull request, and it did not inspect or anticipate any review conclusion.

Every sentence of learner-facing prose, every worked example, every practice task, every retrieval prompt and every assessment item is written for this lesson. No source's wording, figure, table, dataset, teaching example or assessment item was copied or adapted.

Third-party assets

None. The pack contains no third-party image, figure, dataset or media file.

Original assets

Two declarative diagrams, both authored for this lesson and declared in lesson.json under originalAssets:

  • diagrams/renewal-loop.diagram.json — the five-stage crypt renewal loop, whose closing edge carries the lesson's central relation, that the rate of loss sets the rate that must be replaced.
  • diagrams/one-driver-many-outcomes.diagram.json — a concept map in which the same driver mutation appears on the path to a clone in working tissue and on the path to growth that does not end, with two limiting edges from what the tissue does.

Both are bounded JSON with every relationship declared as an explicit edge, and both carry a longDescription that states the same nodes, edges, directions and conclusion as the picture. Neither contains hand-written SVG, script, style, remote reference or active markup.

Source use

Sixteen sources are registered in references.json. Every one was retrieved and read in this run through pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/, which the project source-access ledger records as allowed and which was consulted before any retrieval. No login, paywall or access control was bypassed anywhere, and no source recorded as human-only or excluded was opened.

Every use is factual-reference on the basis facts-only-original-expression. Several of the sources are conventionally copyrighted or carry non-commercial or share-alike licences that this project does not accept for adaptation, which is precisely why nothing is adapted: the facts were read and the expression is this lesson's own.

Four of the sixteen were established for this block by earlier lessons. source-nguyen-colonic-crypt, source-vanderwath-crypt-model, source-benoit-crypt-integrins, source-segawa-flippases and source-parker-apc-recruitment are carried forward, and this run re-retrieved and re-verified each of them against the statements it uses rather than relying on the earlier packs' records. That re-verification found one addition worth recording: the human intestinal crypt review already in the block states that integrin receptors have a central role in controlling anoikis in this tissue, which lets the lesson locate attachment-dependent survival in the colonic crypt rather than only in a cultured kidney line.

Three access findings from this run are appended to site/agent/source-access-ledger.json so the next author inherits them:

  • europepmc.org returns HTTP 403 on /robots.txt, so its access terms could not be established and it is recorded as excluded on the same grounds as an unresolvable host, not on any finding about its terms.
  • eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov was used twice, for bibliographic identifier resolution only, before its robots file was requested; that request was redirected to an NCBI misuse notice, so its terms could not be read. It is recorded as restricted, it is the source of no claim in this pack, and every identifier it returned was confirmed on pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov itself.
  • A pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/pmid/... redirect form returned a challenge page. Nothing was taken from it and the article was read at its canonical article path instead.

The parallel dependency on PREM-BIO-008

This lesson declares topic-cell-biology-cell-cycle-mitosis as a graph prerequisite. The pack teaching that outcome, PREM-BIO-008, was being authored at the same time as this one and could not be read.

The lesson therefore does not summarise, characterise or anticipate PREM-BIO-008 anywhere. PREM-BIO-008 owns cell-cycle control, mitosis, chromosome segregation, cytokinesis, the checkpoints and stem-cell renewal in the crypt, and the pack says so in learner-facing prose in a dedicated callout in scene 1 and again in scene 5, and in the scope field of claim-damage-checkpoint-minimum.

What this lesson borrows is one statement and no more: that a cell can be held in arrest in response to DNA-damage signals long enough to repair its genome before continuing through the cycle. That statement is sourced independently, to a 2014 review of p53 (source-bieging-p53-suppression), and not inferred from what PREM-BIO-008 might say. An earlier draft also borrowed a cell-cycle duration figure; it was removed because the argument does not need it and because the figure sits inside PREM-BIO-008's territory.

Prior lessons in this block

The pack adopts and does not redefine: the crypt architecture, cell count and renewal intervals from PREM-BIO-001 and PREM-BIO-006; the steady-state estimate of about 175 cells a day per crypt from PREM-BIO-001, carried forward with that lesson's own caveat that it is a population rate and not a per-cell lifetime; the phosphatidylserine eat-me signal from PREM-BIO-004; the Wnt gradient, the destruction complex, APC and the conclusion that a cell with damaged APC reports crypt-base position at every height from PREM-BIO-006; and the basal integrin attachment, the junction map and the statement that an enterocyte never leaves the sheet from PREM-BIO-007.

Three deliberate restraints follow from that. Apoptosis at the crypt top was already asserted in the block by PREM-BIO-007's claim-crypt-context, so this lesson adopts that claim's source rather than minting a rival account. The migration mechanism PREM-BIO-007 left open is left open. And the unsettled Wnt inhibition mechanism PREM-BIO-006 left open is not touched.

The glossary adds seventeen terms new to the corpus and repeats one, basement membrane, with an alignment block declaring relation adopt to PREM-BIO-007, because attachment to that specific structure is the survival condition scene 3 turns on. No alias in the glossary is a part standing for a whole or a narrower term standing for a broader one: apoptosis carries no alias precisely because programmed cell death is the wider category and not a synonym, and p53 carries no alias because TP53 is the gene and p53 the protein.

Boundary

This is the most health-sensitive lesson in the block and it is written accordingly.

Every clinical or disease statement is scoped as teaching material. Boundary callouts appear in scene 1, in scene 6 beside the normal-tissue mutation study, and at the head of the clinical wrap-up. The lesson states no diagnosis, no prognosis, no staging, no treatment, no screening or monitoring recommendation, no risk counselling and no personal risk estimate, and it contains no dose, threshold, interval or diagnostic criterion. Clinical oncology management is excluded by this module's syllabus and is not discussed. Population figures are presented as properties of studied groups and are explicitly not anyone's personal risk, following the precedent PREM-BIO-006 set for the same 93 per cent figure.

The tissue described in the clinical wrap-up, and every finding and preparation in the practice scene, are constructed for this lesson from sourced features. None is a real specimen, a real report or a real person, and each says so.

Cancer claims are marked health-sensitive in claims.json: eleven of the twenty-nine claims carry that risk level. No war or conflict metaphor is used anywhere in the pack, and no framing of the material as a struggle, a defeat or a victory.

Stated limitations

Recorded here because a reviewer should not have to find them.

The clearest evidence that normal, functioning tissue carries driver mutations under positive selection comes from sun-exposed eyelid epidermis in four donors aged 55 to 73. It is skin, not colon, and four donors. This pack holds no equivalent dataset for the human colon: the obvious candidate study of normal colorectal crypts is not deposited in PMC, and Europe PMC could not be used because its access terms could not be established. The lesson therefore presents its extension of that finding to colonic crypts explicitly as a use of the model rather than as a reported measurement, in prose, in the retrieval check that does it, and in the uncertainty field of claim-drivers-in-normal-tissue.

Whether shedding at an intestinal surface is caused by detachment or preceded by death is not known, and the review that examines it most closely says so while reporting evidence on both sides. The lesson leaves it open and no assessment key depends on it being settled.

Which of p53's three responses carries its tumour-suppressing effect is unresolved and tissue-dependent, and the lesson keys nothing to it.

The per-villus shedding estimate and the gap-sealing interval are small-intestinal figures, used for the mechanism and the sense of scale they give, and not transferred to the colon.

The rate arithmetic in scene 5 and in the practice scene is the lesson's own illustration of what a balance relation implies. No source calculates a tolerable mismatch between production and loss, and the example states its assumptions, names the one doing the most work, and says which direction its estimate errs in.

Adjudication repairs to the 0.1.0 candidate

The academic review returned request-changes with six major findings and three minor, one of which was a verification note confirming every calculation in the pack; the learning-design review approved with five notes. All eight actionable findings were repaired in one pass and none was declined.

A logic error at the centre of an objective. The objective required the learner to explain why a driver mutation is "necessary and not sufficient" for cancer. The evidence — driver mutations under positive selection in normal, working tissue — refutes sufficiency and says nothing about necessity. The pack's own assessment already said necessity was untouched, which is a different statement from necessity being shown. The objective now asks the learner to state what the evidence does and does not settle, which is the harder and the correct question.

Three claims reached past their sources, and all three are the same failure in different places.

  • The APC claim built a chain from a measured result to an unmeasured outcome. What the sources show is that reorientation of the destruction complex towards a Wnt cue needs full-length APC in cultured colon epithelial cells, so a damaged-APC cell's readout is decoupled from the gradient. That such a cell divides at every height, never differentiates, and fails to depart was not measured. The claim is narrowed to the decoupling, its support downgraded to inference, and the rest is stated as this lesson's reading wherever it appears.
  • The concept map asserted that attachment, the death programme and the crowding response were intact and were what kept a clone benign. The normal-skin study measured mutation and clonal selection and found gross tissue function preserved; it did not measure those three controls. The map now says the tissue still works and that which controls held was not measured, and it names the context it does not draw: immune surveillance, stroma, lineage, and which variant.
  • The clinical case concluded that the removal control had failed because density was raised and no extrusion event was visible. A fixed section cannot measure a rate, and an unobserved event is consistent with a failed mechanism and with a working one too slow to catch. The case now concludes one control demonstrably given way, one under suspicion, and two holding, and says what a demonstration would need.

A linear illustration was turned into a forecast. The rate model was described as a floor because retained cells would divide and make real growth faster. Retained cells may not divide, and as cells accumulate, production, extrusion, differentiation, death and the geometry all change with density, which can accelerate the accumulation, slow it, stop it or reverse it. The model now shows what a small persistent mismatch is capable of over a year and explicitly does not predict what a crypt would do.

An answer key marked a defensible answer wrong. The senescence item required every senescent cell to be secreting the listed programme.
